minutes.headline: Sewer Commission raised its capital transfer to 250,000 after a pump station repair, and kept the 16% rate increase.
minutes.summary: The commission heard about urgent repairs at the Mass One pump station, where suction lines are corroded and the force main is deteriorating, and that Dana Street is in similar shape. It voted a capital transfer from retained earnings, then reconsidered when Dave McDonald joined and raised it to 250,000. It also approved minutes and warrant articles, kept the rate, and discussed the business manager's job rating dispute with the Personnel Committee.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to reconsider its first capital transfer from retained earnings, then approved a larger transfer for pump station needs.
The commission first voted to move more into capital from retained earnings, after hearing about urgent repairs at the Mass One pump station.
The commission kept the earlier 16% rate increase and said the rate would be revisited next year.
The commission adopted the warrant articles as written, with figures to be filled in later, and set a public hearing on sewer connection charge regulations for March 26.
The business manager said leftover funds from the current fiscal year would be encumbered for repairs, avoiding a town meeting vote.

why_it_matters: Sewer repairs are paid from sewer rates and retained earnings, so a larger capital transfer and a kept rate increase bear on sewer bills for connected households.
Drawing on retained earnings for pump station work leaves less in reserve for later repairs, and the Dana Street pumps and 145 remaining manholes are still to be dealt with.
watch_next: March 26 public hearing on the sewer connection charge regulations.
March 12 commission meeting, and the figures still to be filled into the sewer warrant articles.
